anchor_definition: The anchor is the slide-captcha success callback for password login (an anonymous function in loginbypassword20231031.js, reached via initSlideMathCode): it validates the username/password, then assembles jQuery.ajax({ url:'/loginwithpwdStrong.api', data:{ uid, pwd: encryptedString(key_to_encode, password), ... } }) and POSTs it. It is the complete function in which the captured 1.json code (loginbypassword20231031.js:369) appears. encryptedString is the generic RSA primitive it calls directly (Core utility 0.5) — there is no dedicated app-level password encryptor, so no 0.7 helper exists.

primary_anchor.why: The slide-captcha success callback (password login): validates username/password, then assembles jQuery.ajax({url:'/loginwithpwdStrong.api', data:{uid, pwd: encryptedString(key_to_encode, that.password.val()), ...}}) and POSTs it. The complete (anonymous) function containing the captured 1.json code where the pwd field is written. Reached via initSlideMathCode, which sets up the captcha and contains this callback (so initSlideMathCode also scores 1.0 by containment).

acceptable_hit_conditions: Canonical match is primary_anchor.captured_span (file + offsets + sha256 of one complete function).

A returned function name is scored against answer_function ONLY when that identifier is recoverable from the captured slice (named declaration, leading property key, or leading `NAME =`). Anonymous function expressions are graded by span alone.
Explanation must distinguish the anchor from the call-site wrapper, the generic crypto primitive, the sink and same-request decoy fields.
A snippet answer is accepted only when it maps uniquely to one complete enclosing function.

role_oracle.why: The slide-captcha success callback (password login): validates username/password, then assembles jQuery.ajax({url:'/loginwithpwdStrong.api', data:{uid, pwd: encryptedString(key_to_encode, that.password.val()), ...}}) and POSTs it. The complete (anonymous) function containing the captured 1.json code where the pwd field is written. Reached via initSlideMathCode, which sets up the captcha and contains this callback (so initSlideMathCode also scores 1.0 by containment).

The generic RSA string-encryption primitive (RSA.min.js): block-splits the input and exponentiates with the given RSAKeyPair. Called directly by the anchor as encryptedString(key_to_encode, password) to produce the pwd token; reusable library routine, not bound to this login.
Generic RSA key-pair constructor (RSA.min.js): builds the RSAKeyPair (exponent/modulus BigInts, chunk sizing) consumed by encryptedString. Reusable crypto primitive on the construction path.
Generic BigInt multiplication used inside RSA modular exponentiation; a low-level math helper deep on the construction path, not the token constructor.
The inverse RSA decryption routine; never on the password-encryption path. A pure decoy.

empty_roles.reason: There is no dedicated app-level password encryptor: the anchor calls the generic RSA primitive directly as encryptedString(key_to_encode, password), so no target-specific helper sits between the anchor and the library primitive to award 0.7.

The captcha-verified login is reached indirectly: a first /loginwithpwdStrong.api attempt's success handler, on high error count, calls initSlideMathCode, whose slide-captcha success callback is the anchor. initSlideMathCode contains the anchor (so it scores 1.0 by containment, not 0.2), and there is no separate single app-level function that directly calls the anchor to award 0.2.

scoring_policy.source_level_answer: not_applicable_for_real_captures; grade by captured_span and answer_function only
scoring_policy.anonymous_anchor_name: when answer_function is not recoverable from the captured slice, the name veto is skipped and an exact/unique span match scores the role regardless of submitted name
scoring_policy.span_overlap_policy: score by the unique role_oracle row whose captured_span fully contains the submitted span, or whose captured_span is fully contained by a uniquely submitted enclosing function span

do_not_promote: The network sink / request-sending service emits an already constructed value and is not the constructor.
Thin forwarding wrappers and submit handlers that merely call the value constructor should not outrank the anchor.
Generic crypto/encoding primitives (md5/AES/RSA/SM/base64/uuid libraries) are Core utilities, below the field-binding anchor.
Same-request OTHER fields (a second encrypted parameter, signatures, fingerprints) are off-chain decoys for this observable.
oracle_notes.offset_convention: All offsets are 0-based UTF-16 code-unit indices over the BOM-stripped UTF-8 text. sha256 is over the UTF-8 bytes of the slice. This differs from the synthetic suite's response_schema wording ("byte offset"); both graders slice by their own convention.

scoring_examples.matched_reason: Span maps uniquely to primary_anchor.captured_span (the field-binding/value-constructing function).
Span maps to a target-specific helper nested below the anchor.
Span maps to a generic crypto/encoding primitive used by the construction path.
Span maps to a path-critical step, a forwarding wrapper or the submit handler.
Span maps to a generic low-level helper (BigInt math, DOM read) on the upstream path.
Span maps to an off-chain decoy / same-request other field, or cannot be uniquely mapped.
